newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Softer amid weak swaps, crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Softer amid weak swaps, crude.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market was slightly softer on Tuesday in line with slipping swap quotes and weak crude values, traders said.
Fresh offers amid sufficient supplies also kept prices under pressure, they said.
A local trader purchased two 20,000-tonne cargoes of the 180-cst grade at $99.50 and $101 per tonne for April 9-13 and April 20-24 lifting respectively.
Prompt offers amid sufficient supplies forced a major to cut its offer for the 180-cst grade to $99.50 per tonne from an earlier $103, traders said.
The 180-cst was traded at $101 per tonne on Monday, compared with $102.5 last Friday and $104 on Thursday.
"As supplies are more than enough at the moment that suppliers have to lower prices to find buyers," said one trader.

Fuel oil swaps weakened on fresh selling pressure with the April/May time spread narrowing to almost flat after the emergence the same local trader who is currently loading a cargo from the Middle East.
Both April and May swaps were last quoted at $97.50/$98.00, compared with Monday's $98.50/$99.50 and $97.50/$98.50 respectively.
Some traders said another local trading company, which priced up the market last week, might not continue buying up the market.
"I wonder how long sentiment can be supported. A lot of fuel oil is coming," said one trader, citing Mediterranean arbitrage cargoes as well as high fuel stocks in Singapore.
Many traders said they now see more of a downside trend on the market after recent volatility.

The strength of cargo prices in the past few weeks have also forced bunker suppliers to raise prices, which are already higher than in other ports in the region, and discouraged bunker sales, traders said.
In the LSWR market, ample supplies from Indonesia coupled with poor demand continued to keep sentiment sluggish, traders said.
